display_name: DeepSeek V4 family reaches general availability

display_name: DeepReinforce releases the open-weight Ornith-1.5 family

Vendor-reported (five-run-avg): the 397B scores 85.1 Terminal-Bench 2.1 and 56.0 DeepSWE, which Ornith puts on par with Claude Opus 4.8 (85.0 / 59.0).

display_name: Meta releases Muse Spark 1.2 and Muse Code

text: GLM 4.5V's OpenRouter row dropped the 2026-12-31 expiration date it carried in the previous snapshot, so the registry's expiration-date rule now derives `active` instead of `deprecated` — a metadata correction on an otherwise unchanged row (pricing and context identical in both snapshots), not a new release. It matters only for the status badge: the catalog no longer shows the model as deprecated.

Kimi K2.5's OpenRouter row cleared the 2026-08-31 expiration date it carried in the 2026-08-30 snapshot, on the day that date fell due, so the registry's expiration-date rule derives `active` where it derived `deprecated` — had the date stayed, that same rule would have derived `retired` from 2026-09-01. It matters more than a badge: the derived catalog row now reads `active` while the joined entry `model/moonshotai-kimi-k2-5` still declares `status: deprecated`, renders its feed-bound `expiration_date` as `not published`, and opens on the claim that this row carries a death date almost none do — the two surfaces now disagree about the same model.

excerpt.description: Cohere - Cohere released Parse 5 (parse-v5.0), a 2.3B document-intelligence vision-language model that converts PDFs, slides, and images into structured Markdown with tables, forms, and bounding boxes, across nine languages. Priced at $1.50 per 1,000 pages via API, with Model Vault, SageMaker, and Azure availability. Positioned on price-to-performance.
excerpt.title: Cohere releases Parse 5 document-intelligence VLM

display_name: Z.ai surfaces GLM-5.2 Turbo fast-serving tier

excerpt.description: Z.ai (Zhipu AI) - Z.ai's GLM-5.2 Turbo (API id glm-5.2-fast) surfaced as a speed-optimized hosted serving tier of GLM-5.2, carrying the 1M-token context and served through Z.ai and SCX.ai at premium fast-tier pricing (~$1.99 in / $6.16 out per Mtok). Parameter count, architecture detail, and any open-weight release for the Turbo tier are undisclosed.
excerpt.title: Z.ai surfaces GLM-5.2 Turbo fast-serving tier

excerpt.description: Alibaba (Qwen) - Alibaba released Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, an open-weight 125B/6B sparse MoE previewing the Qwen4 architecture (Gated-DeltaNet + Qwen Sparse Attention, n-gram embedding, multi-token prediction). Native 262K context extensible to 1M via YaRN; weights under the Qwen Community License 1.0. Status: preview.
excerpt.title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Qwen4 preview)

excerpt.description: IBM - The smallest Granite 4.2 model (~4B on Hugging Face), aimed at local / edge deployment, with the family's thinking / non-thinking switch and native tool calling. Open weights on Hugging Face, Ollama, and GitHub.
excerpt.title: IBM Granite 4.2 3B released (Apache-2.0)

display_name: Thomson Reuters launches its in-house frontier model, Thomson

excerpt.description: Thomson Reuters - Thomson Reuters announced Thomson, its first in-house proprietary LLM, trained on decades of Westlaw, Practical Law, Checkpoint, and Reuters content to a "Fiduciary-Grade" standard (~$40M training investment). First deployed inside Tabular Analysis in CoCounsel Legal; size, architecture, and context are undisclosed, and a smaller open-weight variant is being released for academic use. Status: preview.
excerpt.title: Thomson Reuters launches its in-house frontier model, Thomson

display_name: Alibaba launches the managed Qwen3.8-Flash API

excerpt.description: Alibaba (Qwen) - Alibaba announced Qwen3.8-Flash, the productionized, managed Qwen Cloud API twin of the open-weight Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, running the same Qwen4-preview MoE architecture. Defaults to a 1M-token context with built-in tools; list pricing $0.15 input / $0.47 output per Mtok. Recorded proprietary/API-only.
excerpt.title: Alibaba launches the managed Qwen3.8-Flash API

display_name: GLM-5.3 open weights released under a bespoke license

excerpt.description: Z.ai (Zhipu AI) - Z.ai published GLM-5.3's open weights on Hugging Face (zai-org/GLM-5.3) after a roughly two-week safety review it attributed to unexpectedly strong multi-stage exploit-chaining found during evaluation. The weights ship under a bespoke "GLM-5.3 License" — MIT-equivalent for most users, but companies with >$10B revenue over any consecutive 12 months must pass Z.AI's security review before commercial Model-as-a-Service use. GLM-5.3-Flash remains plain MIT.
excerpt.title: GLM-5.3 open weights released under a bespoke license

excerpt.description: Tencent Hunyuan - Tencent Hunyuan released and open-sourced Hy4 preview under Apache-2.0 — a 770B-total / 49B-active MoE flagship with a 1M-token context, aimed at long-horizon software engineering, office/financial analysis, and scientific work. Weights and an FP8 variant on Hugging Face; also served via Tencent Cloud TokenHub and OpenRouter. Preview stage; vendor figures unverified at launch.
excerpt.title: Tencent open-sources Hy4 preview (770B MoE)

display_name: DeepSeek pins the V4-Pro GA build as 0813

excerpt.description: DeepSeek - DeepSeek pinned the dated GA build behind its deepseek-v4-pro API id (OpenRouter listing dated Aug 12 2026), the Pro-tier counterpart to V4-Flash-0731. Keeps the V4-Pro 1.6T/49B MoE architecture and 1M-token context; cache-heavy list pricing. Recorded proprietary/API-only (no confirmed separate 0813 open-weight repo).
excerpt.title: DeepSeek pins the V4-Pro GA build as 0813

excerpt.description: Z.ai (Zhipu AI) - Z.ai released GLM-5.3-Flash, a 320B-total / 18B-active natively multimodal MoE with a 1M-token context and MIT-licensed open weights (zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash), priced roughly 10x cheaper on input than the text-only GLM-5.3 flagship. Vision is integrated into the coding/agent loop. Vendor benchmarks unverified at launch.
excerpt.title: Z.ai releases GLM-5.3-Flash

excerpt.description: IBM - The mid-size member of IBM's Granite 4.2 open reasoning family (~9B on Hugging Face): a dense decoder-only transformer trained to call tools and act inside sandboxed environments for software-engineering, terminal, and search tasks. Open weights on Hugging Face, Ollama, and GitHub.
excerpt.title: IBM Granite 4.2 8B released (Apache-2.0)

display_name: IBM releases the Granite 4.2 open reasoning family

excerpt.description: IBM - IBM released Granite 4.2 in 3B, 8B, and 30B sizes under Apache-2.0 — dense decoder-only models with a thinking / non-thinking switch and low-effort reasoning mode, pre-trained on ~15T tokens and post-trained with multi-stage RL for agentic tool use. The 30B reports ~57 on SWE-bench Verified. Open weights on Hugging Face, Ollama, and GitHub.
excerpt.title: IBM releases the Granite 4.2 open reasoning family

text: Nex-N2-Mini's OpenRouter row gained the `2026-09-04` expiration_date it did not carry in the 2026-08-31 snapshot, so the registry's expiration-date rule (absent -> active, within 365 days -> deprecated) now derives `deprecated` where it derived `active` — a genuine lifecycle event, unlike the two earlier status flips on this source, both of which were dropped expiration dates, not new deprecations. It matters: the stub `model/nex-agi-nex-n2-mini` presents `deprecated` (feed-bound `$status`) on its built page, its timeline carries the mechanically appended `deprecated` event dated 2026-09-01, and the same rule derives `retired` once 2026-09-04 passes.

Nex-N2-Pro's OpenRouter row gained an `expiration_date` of `2026-09-04` that it did not carry in the 2026-08-31 snapshot, so the registry's expiration-date rule (absent -> active, within 365 days -> deprecated) now derives `deprecated` where it previously derived `active` — a real lifecycle event: the row's first recorded status flip, so it cannot be a metadata correction of a dropped date. It matters: the stub `model/nex-agi-nex-n2-pro` renders `deprecated` on its built page through the feed-bound `$status` fact, its timeline carries the mechanically appended `deprecated` event dated 2026-09-01, and the same rule derives `retired` once 2026-09-04 passes.

On 2026-09-02 the OpenRouter row for `z-ai/glm-4.5v` again carries `expiration_date: 2026-12-31` (absent from the 2026-09-01 snapshot), so this site's expiration-date rule re-derives the status as `deprecated` — a scheduled end-of-life date, not a vendor retirement: OpenRouter's API reference defines `expiration_date` as "the date after which the model may be removed", and both of the model's OpenRouter endpoints (Z.AI, Novita) still serve it as of 2026-09-02, so it remains callable for now. It matters as a migration cue rather than an outage — plan around the 2026-12-31 removal date, and the current next-generation vision model in Z.ai's line is the active `z-ai/glm-4.6v` (131K context, $0.30/$0.90 per 1M vs GLM-4.5V's $0.60/$1.80 on OpenRouter).
